title: Read a file's size in the terminal and write it into a note in Mousepad

capabilities.why: Mousepad and Xfce's terminal, and xdotool, which setup places their windows with.
argv: command -v mousepad && command -v xfce4-terminal && command -v xdotool

setup.why: Make the run's folder with a data file of {{size}} bytes and an empty note.
Open Xfce's terminal in the run's folder.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && exec xfce4-terminal --disable-server --working-directory=/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}

setup.why: Wait for the terminal's window (20 s at most) and give it the left half of the screen.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class xfce4-terminal | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no terminal window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $((WIDTH / 2)) $HEIGHT

setup.why: Open the empty note in Mousepad.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && exec mousepad /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/notes-{{nonce}}.txt

setup.why: Wait for Mousepad's window (20 s at most), give it the right half of the screen, and put the pointer on it: with no window manager, keys go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class mousepad | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no Mousepad window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); h=$((WIDTH / 2)); xdotool windowmove $w $h 0 windowsize $w $h $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((h + h / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); sleep 1

instruction: Use the terminal (left) to find the size in bytes of /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/data-{{nonce}}.bin. Then, in Mousepad (right), where notes-{{nonce}}.txt is open, write the line "size: <the size in bytes>" (just the number, such as size: 1234) and save the file. This desktop has no window manager: keys go to the window under the mouse pointer.

checks.why: The saved note holds the one line with the data file's size, {{size}} bytes (blank space around it aside). The size is picked per seed and setup's note is empty, so an agent that does nothing fails, and one that guesses can't know it.

teardown.why: Close Mousepad and the terminal (KILL: Mousepad holds on to a changed document on TERM), and delete the run's folder.

argv: pkill -9 -x mousepad; pkill -9 -x xfce4-terminal; rm -rf /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; true

oracle.why: The pointer is on Mousepad: type the line and Save (Ctrl+S); the note has a name, so no dialog. The oracle knows the size, so it does not use the terminal: it proves the check reads the saved note, and that the editor's half of the path works.
